solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do books take on concave shape when gathering dust?

indicators.note: gathering means collecting something up inside, so the shape word closes around the dust word

parts.note: to cup something is to make it take on a hollow, concave shape
ash is the dusty residue left by burning

explanation.surface: A picture of old ledgers on a shelf warping out of shape as they sit collecting dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do books' looks like a noun phrase, but it is an instruction: to do the books in a shop at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash up is to total the day's takings and reconcile the accounts, which is doing the books.

clue.text: Worry this Conservative PM won't, drinking cordial on the House

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so the shuffled letters hold the cordial inside them
to worry is to tug and shake something about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: lime is a classic cordial, a sweet fruit drink diluted with water

explanation.surface: A Conservative Prime Minister fretting over something they refuse to do while sipping a soft drink in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' with its capital suggests Parliament, but 'on the house' is the idiom for free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sent with compliments is given free, as a courtesy, just as a drink on the house costs the customer nothing.

clue.text: Two employees on counter accepting that was spiteful

indicators.note: on counter says the hidden letters are read backwards
accepting means the phrase takes the answer's letters in, holding them within its words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Two shop workers behind a counter putting up with a nasty remark from a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'accepting' into the definition; it is the signal that the two words hold the letters, leaving 'that was spiteful' as the definition, an exclamation in reply to a catty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: People mimic a cat's cry to point out a catty, spiteful remark, so the word comments that the remark was spiteful.

clue.text: A hand getting up

parts.note: 'a hand' is a round of applause, and here the audience gets up out of their seats to give it

explanation.walkthrough: 'A hand getting up' reads like a raised hand, but giving someone a hand means applauding them.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience rising to its feet while clapping is the highest form of applause a performer can receive.

clue.text: A half-day on run after having left penal colony

indicators.note: after says the rest of the pieces follow the word for left
on says the half-day piece comes next to the run piece, joined on after it

parts.note: port is the nautical word for left
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
THUR is half of the name THURSDAY, a day

explanation.surface: Someone who has walked out of a penal colony spends half a day on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Arthur in Tasmania was a notorious convict settlement in the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Arthur was a British prison settlement in Tasmania where transported convicts were held.

clue.text: Quickly appreciating performance?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: very fast, a British informal idiom
second meaning, read literally: fond of the people clapping, as a performer would be

explanation.walkthrough: 'Like the clappers' is British slang for very fast; the second reading takes 'like' as a verb, enjoying the applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Running like the clappers means going at great speed, while a performer who likes the clappers enjoys the audience's applause.

clue.text: Man hopeless securing husband's shed

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly in place, so the hopeless words keep the husband inside them

parts.note: something hopeless is no use
H is the abbreviation for husband, used in family trees; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A useless man has locked his husband in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb, as in shedding something, but it is the outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A henhouse is a small hut where chickens are kept, a kind of shed.

clue.text: Overcoming condition, mum's home clear

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum

indicators.note: the home word comes over and around the condition word, enclosing it

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from an illness has been given the all-clear to leave their mother's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest as an adjective means obvious or plainly evident, the same as clear in 'it is clear that'.

clue.text: One's first Scouse bird — who could ask for more!

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first letter of One
the Liver bird is the emblem of Liverpool, and Scouse means from Liverpool

explanation.surface: A Liverpudlian's first pet bird is so delightful that nobody could want anything more.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liver bird is the mythical bird that is Liverpool's symbol, perched on the Royal Liver Building.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's novel, the workhouse orphan Oliver Twist famously holds out his bowl and asks for more gruel.

clue.text: Doctor Who they hadn't cut for screening reasons

indicators.note: screening means hiding something behind or within, so the shuffled letters enclose the cutting word
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: An episode of Doctor Who that the broadcaster had not trimmed before it was shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' reads as the TV series, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal working on the letters of WHO THEY HADNT; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The how and the why of something are its method and its causes, the explanations or reasons behind it.

clue.text: Sister's inspiring grave by church that is more prominently marked

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the sister abbreviation takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for Sister

indicators.note: by means next to, so the church piece sits beside the grave piece

parts.note: a plot is a burial plot, a grave
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A nun drawing inspiration from a grave beside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something splotchier has more blotches, larger and more noticeable patches of colour on it.

clue.text: Friend and "colleague" initially welcome stay in bed?

indicators.note: initially says just the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first letter of colleague
hi is a word of greeting or welcome
to nap late is to stay dozing in bed in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone greeting a friend and workmate who wants a lie-in.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so it means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang, china plate stands for mate, a pal or companion.

clue.text: Respect missing on occasion

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the word for respect is without these two letters

parts.note: to honour someone is to respect them

explanation.surface: Failing to show respect on some particular occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour can mean a particular time or moment, as in 'the hour of need', an occasion.

clue.text: The 7 being out of bounds: one's gone 21

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the HENHOUSE (7 down) creature, a chicken, that no longer bounds or springs about
second meaning: someone who is no longer young, who has become PAST IT (21 across)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' suggests a forbidden area, but bounds are leaps: a chicken with no spring in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone no spring chicken is an idiom saying they are no longer young, getting on in years.

clue.text: Two birds cycling — only one can fly high

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so a letter moves from the front to the back

parts.note: the dove and the rhea are two birds

explanation.surface: Two birds out for a bike ride, though only one of them could fly instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only one can fly' confirms the birds: a dove flies, but the rhea, a large South American bird like an ostrich, cannot.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead means above one's head, up in the sky, so high up.

clue.text: Food shop's very short supply?

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the word for supply is without the word very

parts.note: a delivery is a supply of goods

explanation.surface: A shop that is running very low on stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Dissenting small-screen song and dance about sacking director

indicators.note: about means around, so the trimmed dance goes round the screen and song pieces
sacking means dismissing, so the director letter is removed from dance

parts.note: taken as written
TV is the small screen, as opposed to cinema
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to a TV musical number that went ahead after its director was fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song and dance' reads as one phrase meaning fuss, but the song and the dance are separate pieces; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at variance is to be in disagreement or conflict, which is what dissenting parties are.

clue.text: Spirit soaring, is allowed to leave college

indicators.note: in a down answer soaring means rising upward, so the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: can means is allowed, as in 'you can go'
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A student whose spirits lift when permitted to leave college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like mood, but it is the alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy from the Cognac region of France, a distilled alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Novel Pi tells involving tiger — the protagonists in a battle for survival

definitions.text: the protagonists in a battle for survival

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Life of Pi is a novel in which the boy Pi tells of his struggle to survive in a lifeboat with a tiger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' points to Life of Pi, but it is the anagram signal; 'involving' is a link. The pigs survive the wolf trying to blow their houses down.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale, three young pigs fight to survive a wolf that wants to eat them.

clue.text: Very much like a Biblical spouse?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: describing ... wife, the unnamed spouse of Lot in Genesis

explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and was turned into a pillar of salt; she is never named, only called Lot's.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots means a great deal, as in 'lots better', while Lot's is how the Bible identifies his wife.

clue.text: The case of pickpocket smuggling something sparkling over the hill

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden, so the outer letters hold the wine inside
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A pickpocket hiding a bottle of fizz in a case, who is getting too old for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is too old to do things well, the idiom being over the hill, beyond their best years.

clue.text: Rash sanction controlling uranium consumption about America

indicators.note: controlling means holding in check, so the approval word contains the other pieces

parts.note: to OK something is to sanction or approve it
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
TB, tuberculosis, was once called consumption
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A hasty decision to restrict uranium use around America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective meaning hasty, but it is the skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak can be a sudden eruption of spots on the skin, which is a rash.
